title: ONLYOFFICE Docs Configuration Schema
description:
Complete configuration schema with scope markers for validation and documentation.

Custom annotation `x-tenantOverride` (boolean):
- `true`  — setting this key in a per-tenant `config.json` is safe and either takes effect (supported) or is silently ignored without breaking anything (deprecated/unused).
- `false` — setting this key per-tenant either has no effect (global-only), takes effect only under specific conditions (conditional), or causes a silent inconsistency with shared/global state (unsafe). Refer to `docs/tenant-config-overrides.md` for the specific category and operational notes.

The annotation covers every leaf-key present in `default.json` plus the `persistentStorage` parent (annotated once, since its body inherits from `storage`). The detailed evidence trail is in `docs/tenant-config-override-audit.md`.

allowBrowserProxy.description: Enables the unmatched-target relay mode inside /ai-proxy: when the target matches no configured provider, the request is forwarded as-is (with the client's own credentials) to bypass CORS. The server injects no credentials; the caller still needs a valid session JWT; the target stays untrusted and uses the normal externalRequest private-IP filtering. On by default to support browser-configured MCP and web search; set to false to keep unmatched targets denied with 403.

notification.description: The notification system configuration for license expiration and limits warnings.
notification.x-section-intro:
These parameters configure the notification settings.

Notifications with the following event types and content are sent:

- 70% of the [connection quota](./license.md#licensewarning_limit_percents) (quota of unique users) is exceeded.

  License connection limit warning: *"Attention! You have reached 70% of the connections limit set by your license."*

- The connection quota (quota of unique users) is reached.

  License connection limit warning: *"Attention! You have reached 100% of the connection limit set by your license."*

- 30 days before the [license expires](./license.md#licensewarning_license_expiration).

  License expiration warning: *"Attention! Your license is about to expire on September 8, 2024. Upon reaching this date, you will no longer be entitled to receive personal technical support and install new Docs versions released after this date."*

- The license has expired.

  License connection limit warning: *"Attention! Your license expired on September 8, 2024. You are no longer entitled to receive personal technical support and install new Docs versions released after this date. Please contact sales@onlyoffice.com to discuss license renewal."*

allowPrivateIPAddress.description: Whether it is allowed to connect private IP address or not. This includes private IP addresses and reserved IP addresses.

allowMetaIPAddress.description: Whether it is allowed to connect meta IP address or not. Meta address can be `0.0.0.0` (IPv4) or `::` (IPv6) - a meta address that routing another address.

allowIPAddressList.description: The IP addresses that are allowed even when they are private. The request-filtering-agent checks this list before its own meta, private and deny checks, so for ordinary outbound requests an entry here outranks everything. It does not permit a WOPI destination: that is decided by `services.CoAuthoring.ipfilter.rules` alone.

denyIPAddressList.description: The IP addresses that are never allowed. For WOPI destinations a deny here outranks every permission, including an `ipfilter.rules` entry naming the same address. For other filtered requests the request-filtering-agent's own precedence applies, where `allowIPAddressList` is checked first; a direct request bypasses the agent entirely.

connectionTimeoutMillis.description: A number of milliseconds to wait for a connection.

idleTimeoutMillis.description: A number of milliseconds a client must remain idle in the pool and not be checked out before it is disconnected from the backend and discarded. Set to 0 to disable automatic disconnection of idle clients.

maxLifetimeSeconds.description: A number of seconds after which a pooled connection is recycled. A running query is never interrupted: the connection is marked as expired and closed when it is returned to the pool. Recycling lets the pool pick up a database failover or an address change and bounds the lifetime of a backend process. Set to 0 to disable recycling.

query_timeout.description: A number of milliseconds before a query call times out on the client side. When it fires, the query is reported as failed and the pool destroys the connection, but the query is not cancelled on the server explicitly. While `statement_timeout` is 0, this is the only limit that keeps a stuck query from holding a pool slot forever. Set to 0 to disable.

statement_timeout.description: A number of milliseconds before the query statement times out on the server side. It is passed in the PostgreSQL startup message, so a connection pooler may reject the connection, silently drop the value or forward it to the backend: PgBouncer rejects it unless the parameter is listed in its `ignore_startup_parameters`, and listing it there makes the pooler drop the value instead of applying it. Behind a pooler set the limit on the database itself, for example `ALTER ROLE onlyoffice SET statement_timeout = '60s'`. Set to 0 to disable, which is the default.

purposeCheck.description: How strictly an inbound token must prove what it is for. It governs the compatibility-sensitive half: the marker heuristic, the closed field sets of `docbuilder` and `command`, and the `operation` claim. `off` - none of them is applied. `validate` - the heuristic rejects browser/session token shapes on the guarded inbox operations (converter, docbuilder, command), a token whose `operation` claim names another operation is rejected, and a sink that serves no named operation rejects any token carrying the claim at all. `strict` - the claim additionally becomes mandatory, but only at the sinks that name an operation (converter, docbuilder, command); the browser, editor-session and download sinks share their tokens with one another and keep accepting claimless ones. `strict` is also the setting that closes a `/docbuilder` request carrying its script in the request body: that script is never covered by the signature, so the claim is the only thing telling such a build apart from any other token that fits the builder field set. An unknown value fails closed at every sink that verifies an integrator token, not only at the three inbox operations. What this setting never relaxes: every sink still enforces the structure its handler reads, including the ban on a `url` in a from-file token, so an empty signed token authorizes nothing at the sinks that name their fields - `browser-open` and `download` are the documented exception, they accept any plain-object payload because a partially signed request is legitimate there, and the from-file endpoints still require the claim on every token they verify - like every other endpoint they do accept an unsigned request when inbound JWT is disabled.
